title: INS Vikrant: A Carrier Built in India

segments.say: Seventy-six per cent. That is how much of INS Vikrant, the largest warship ever built in India, comes from Indian sources.
It is about two hundred and sixty-two metres long, sixty-one metres wide, and weighs about forty-five thousand tonnes. The Navy's own bureau designed it; Cochin Shipyard built it.

anim.title: How planes fly from it
items: Take off up a ski-jump ramp

segments.say: Planes take off up a curved ski-jump ramp and land by hooking arrester wires. The Navy calls this STOBAR.
It can carry up to thirty aircraft, including MiG-29K fighters like this one, and several kinds of helicopter.
Its special steel, about thirty thousand tonnes, came from SAIL. More than five hundred and fifty Indian firms, including about a hundred small businesses, supplied parts.

items.text: the new Vikrant is commissioned at Kochi

segments.say: The name is old. The first Vikrant retired in nineteen ninety-seven; the new one was commissioned at Kochi in September twenty twenty-two.
For GS Three, Vikrant is the case study for defence indigenisation: design, steel and shipbuilding, all done at home.

sources: PIB backgrounder, 24 October 2025 (PRID 2182277): commissioned 2 September 2022 at Kochi; 76% indigenous content; 30,000 tonnes of SAIL steel; designed by the Navy's Warship Design Bureau, built by Cochin Shipyard; largest warship built in India; 262.5 m long, 61.6 m wide, about 45,000 tonnes; STOBAR (ski-jump take-off, arrester-wire recovery); up to 30 aircraft including MiG-29K, MiG-29KUB, Kamov-31, MH-60R, Chetak and ALH; named after INS Vikrant (R11), decommissioned 1997; over 550 OEMs and about 100 MSMEs

reviewNote: All facts are from one PIB backgrounder (October 2025).
